name: SHT40-AD1B-R2
title: SHT4x digital relative humidity and temperature sensor, I2C, 1.5 × 1.5 mm DFN
summary: A humidity and temperature sensor family in a 4-pin 1.5 × 1.5 × 0.54 mm open-cavity DFN that reports both readings as 16-bit words with CRC over I2C (up to fast mode plus). It runs from 1.08 to 3.6 V, idles at 80 nA and averages 0.4 µA at one low-repeatability reading per second. Accuracy class sets the part: SHT40 ±1.8 %RH and ±0.2 °C typical, SHT41 intermediate, SHT43 with an ISO 17025 3-point temperature calibration, SHT45 ±1.0 %RH and ±0.1 °C. A built-in heater (20, 110 or 200 mW) clears condensation; options add a polyimide membrane or a peel-off cover. The SHT40-AD1B-R2 is the base-accuracy part at address 0x44 on a 2’500-piece reel.

circuits.title: Typical application circuit
circuits.description: The sensor on an I2C bus run by a microcontroller. SDA and SCL each have a 10 kΩ pull-up to VDD, and a 100 nF capacitor sits across VDD and ground. The part answers at its preset address (0x44 for the SHT40-AD1B).

operation.text: Once VDD has reached its minimum, the part needs at most 1 ms (tPU) before it takes I2C traffic. The supply must not ramp faster than 20 V/ms between its minimum and maximum, or the part may reset. Between 0.6 V and 1.08 V on a static supply the part is in its power-up/down region.

Write command 0xFD to address 0x44, wait 10 ms, then read 6 bytes. Bytes 0 and 1 are the temperature word (high byte first) and byte 2 its CRC; bytes 3 and 4 are the humidity word and byte 5 its CRC. Convert with the equations and clip humidity to 0 … 100 %RH.

The bus follows NXP UM10204 in standard, fast and fast-mode-plus speeds. Every transfer opens with a start condition and closes with a stop; the master ends a read with NACK then stop. A 7-bit address plus a direction bit (0 write, 1 read) selects the part. The address is fixed by the part number: 0x44 (A), 0x45 (B) or 0x46 (C). The part does not stretch the clock: a read header that arrives while it is measuring or heating gets NACK. A result can be read only once; it is cleared after the first acknowledged read header.

Data move as 16-bit words, each sent as two bytes and followed by a CRC-8 byte (polynomial 0x31, init 0xFF, no reflection, no final XOR). A measurement returns temperature first, then humidity. The master may stop a read after any word if it has no use for the checksum.

Three measurement commands pick high, medium or low repeatability. Higher repeatability means less noise, a longer conversion (up to 8.3 ms against 1.6 ms) and more energy per reading; at one reading a second the average current is 2.2, 1.2 or 0.4 µA.
Every part holds a unique serial number written once in production in one-time-programmable memory. Command 0x89 returns it as two 16-bit words, each with its CRC.

Three things reset the part: the soft-reset command 0x94; an I2C general call reset, which is command 0x06 sent to address 0x00 and resets every device on the bus; or removing power, with SCL and SDA also pulled low. A general call reset or a soft reset also stops any command in progress.

An on-package heater runs at 20, 110 or 200 mW (typical at VDD = 3.3 V) for 0.1 s or 1 s, chosen by command. On a heater command the heater turns on and a timer starts; when the timer ends a high-repeatability measurement runs with the heater still on; then the heater turns off and the reading waits to be read. No command turns the heater off, since one second is the longest it stays on. Longer heating takes repeated commands with little idle time between them, and the heater is built for a duty cycle under 10 % of the part's life. Uses include clearing condensation or spray water, which stops the sensor seeing humidity changes, and pulsed heating to avoid creep in long spells at high humidity.

The accuracy figures do not hold while the heater is on, and heat-induced mechanical stress can offset the temperature reading. The die temperature, ambient plus heater rise, must stay at or below 125 °C, so the heater is only run in ambient below 65 °C. At the highest setting the heater draws up to about 75 mA; the part ramps this current in smoothly, but the supply must hold up under it or the sensor can reset.

Best performance is in 5 … 60 °C and 20 … 80 %RH. Long stays outside that range, high humidity above all, can shift the humidity reading for a while (for example +3 %RH after 60 h above 80 %RH); the part drifts back into specification on its own once returned to the normal range. Long exposure to extreme conditions can speed ageing. The part resists volatile organic compounds well, and Sensirion's handling instructions on contamination apply in use as well as in transport and assembly. The specifications are for the bare sensor; Sensirion's design-in guide covers mounting.

Each part is tested and calibrated individually and carries its own serial number. The references used are traceable to NIST through an ISO/IEC 17025 accredited laboratory. The SHT43 gets an individual 3-point temperature calibration at −30 °C, 5 °C and 70 °C, accredited to ISO/IEC 17025:2017 by the Swiss Accreditation Service (SCS 0158); certificates and data per reel come from libellus.sensirion.com.

An open-cavity 4-pin DFN with the humidity opening at the top centre. The silicon die sits on a copper lead frame under an epoxy mold compound; the bottom contacts are Ni/Pd/Au plated and the sides are plain copper. MSL 1 to IPC/JEDEC J-STD-020; the parts are best processed within a year of delivery.

Two lines of laser marking. Line one: a filled dot over pin 1, then SH4 and one character for the accuracy class. Line two: three characters for positions 7, 8 and 9 of the part number (for example AD1), then a three-character batch code. The membrane and cover options carry the same marking, which can be harder to read on the cover option after the cover is removed.

A polyimide membrane, nominally 40 µm thick, covers the opening. It is built to filter particles of 200 nm size, reduces liquid getting in, gives a flat top that can be wiped, and allows use in IP68 conditions. The RH response time is unchanged. Board mounting follows Sensirion's reflow profile and its board-wash and cleaning precautions.

The part ships with a polyimide foil sealing the opening, so conformal coating can be brushed or sprayed over the board without filling the opening. The foil withstands chemicals and high temperature and is peeled off afterwards with tweezers by its non-stick tab. Mounting follows Sensirion's reflow profile.
Qualified to JEDEC JESD47. RoHS and WEEE compliant, free of Pb, Cd and Hg.
